name: RMII routing
question: Land the RMII link as routed, with the two placement changes it needs at the PHY?
why_now:
You asked me to route just the RMII link from the PHY (U501) to the MCU (U401), the board's hardest routing. Every fast route so far has failed some of it.

I routed the ten nets alone with KiCadRoutingTools at the board's own sizes: TXD0/1, TX_EN, RXD0/1, CRS_DV, RX_ER, REF_CLK, MDC and MDIO. The first five runs each failed a different net, and KRT's reachability check said every pad was reachable, so the cause is the geometry at the PHY, not the router. **U401 is not the problem:** every run reached all ten of its balls, which sit in its north-west corner in the outer four rows. Turning the MCU isn't needed.

Two things wall U501 in:

1. **Six parts on the wrong side.** R505, R509, R510 (strap resistors), R507 (MDIO pull-up), TP503 and TP504 (MDC/MDIO test points) sit west of U501. Their pins (RX_ER, CRS_DV and RXD0 on the east and north sides, MDC and MDIO on the north) are elsewhere. Three RX lines detoured west through the strip where the three TX lines start, and whichever line routed last was boxed in. No block holds these parts; the annealer placed them.
2. **Y501 is 0.33 mm from the PHY's RX pins.** The 50 MHz oscillator's courtyard starts 0.33 mm past the end of U501's east pads (pins 18–24), and its keep-out (only its own nets and GND on B and In4) starts inside them. RX pins 19–21 have no way out on the bottom side. Y501 is in the T1S block (k501, D16), so this is a block change.

facts.label: Router settings
facts.value: KRT at its latest commit; 0.15 mm track and clearance; 0.35/0.20 mm vias; F.Cu, In2 (signal window north of y 70) and B.Cu; the judge's preparation and fan-outs of U401 and U501 first; Y401/Y501 keep-outs made via-free for the router (the board's rule forbids other nets' vias there, which KRT doesn't model); MDIO and MDC first, then the eight RMII lines

facts.label: Judged on
facts.value: Only the ten nets' copper copied onto a real copy of main with the moves, zones refilled, KiCad DRC with node60.kicad_dru

facts.label: RMII timing
facts.value: 50 MHz reference clock; data set up 4 ns before and held 2 ns after its edge. 36 mm of length spread is about 0.25 ns

options.name: Move the six parts and Y501, land the routing

images.caption: Today: straps and test points west of U501; Y501 against its east pins
Moved, and routed: straps by their pins, Y501 2 mm east
The ten nets from U501 to U401; dots are vias

measures.label: Nets routed
measures.value: 10 of 10 (TX, RX, CRS_DV, RX_ER, REF_CLK, MDC, MDIO)

measures.label: DRC on the real copy
measures.value: 0 errors, parity 0; no RMII or MDIO connection open

measures.label: Lengths
measures.value: REF_CLK 44 mm; data 43–80 mm (CRS_DV and RX_ER longest, through their straps to the south); MDC 50, MDIO 47

measures.label: Layers
measures.value: In2 carries most of it (about 250 mm); B about 210 mm; F about 110 mm. On F nothing crosses the T1S trunk's line (y 46 between J912 and J903)

measures.label: T1S PHY pair (U501 pins 30/31)
measures.value: The router fails it on main and with RMII in place alike: RMII takes nothing it needs. It stays your hand route (pin 30's margin is 1.2 µm)

measures.label: GND pour under the routes
measures.value: Cut into islands (GND opens 3 → 34); the interior stitching rejoins them (→ 4 on a trial). That is D25's after-routing grid

gains: The hardest link routed, with no MCU turn
Strap stubs off the 50 MHz lines' way
The In3 webs at U401 made robust
costs: The k501 block changes (Y501, R503, R504)
The routes are the router's: CRS_DV and RX_ER take a long way south; tidy them by hand if you like
Needs the interior GND stitching once routing is done

options.name: Moves only, route RMII yourself
options.summary: Land the placement changes (six parts, Y501) and the In3 width fix, and leave the RMII copper to you, using these routes as a guide.
costs: The work done here isn't used

options.name: Turn U401 instead
options.summary: Rotate the MCU so its RMII balls face the PHY. Not tested: it isn't where the routing fails. It would reopen D23's decap block, the In3 1V5 island, the crystal block Y401 and which side every peripheral faces.
costs: Large rework for a problem at the PHY, which it doesn't fix

recommendation.why: The RMII link fails because of placement at the PHY, not at the MCU. Two small moves fix it and all ten nets route with DRC clean on a real copy. A lands that work. B keeps the moves and leaves the copper to you. C answers a question the evidence doesn't ask. On A I land it in one PR: the moves (k501 table updated), the rule areas redrawn, the routed copper locked, the In3 width fix, DRC and the records.

answer: Reply with A, B or C. (D25, the GND stitching, is still open too.)
sources: kicad-cli DRC on a copy of main
